If KnowledgeOS believes H, chooses an H-consistent action, observes an H-consistent outcome, and concludes H was confirmed, this is Self-confirmation -- the dangerous loop Belief -> Action -> Observation -> BeliefStrengthening, which without independent information reinforces its own assumptions. Worked example: recommending Architecture_A because it 'reduces incidents' causes most new projects to adopt A; observed incident reduction is then wrongly attributed to A rather than to the real cause (new projects generally having better engineering practices) -- the system strengthens its own causal hypothesis using data influenced by its own policy." (anchor: "Self-generated evidence and the confirmation loop: Belief->Action->Observation->BeliefStrengthening")
- `[S0942]` types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "The system's policy pi_t changes the distribution of future observations P(O_{t+1}|pi_t), so the data-generating process is not independent of the decision system -- 'this is fundamental'. (anchor: "Policy-induced distribution shift; closed-loop learning Policy->Data->Model->Policy")
- `[S0942]` types=[DISTINCTION, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "Learning M_{t+1}=L(M_t,D_t) may converge M_t->M* or stay in an acceptable region, but convergence alone is insufficient: a system can converge to a wrong model (M_t -> M_wrong), so Learning convergence != Truth. Requires two separate properties Stability(M) and Validity(M): a model can have Stability=True while Validity=False -- 'stable and wrong', described as worse than obvious instability because it may appear trustworthy." (anchor: "Epistemic stability vs epistemic validity; learning convergence != truth; stable-and-wrong is worse than unstable")
- `[S0942]` types=[PRINCIPLE, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "Bayesian framing: supporting evidence updates P(H|E), strong contradictory evidence E- can reduce P(H|E,E-); KnowledgeOS must maintain the possibility of downward belief revision. Rejects Confidence_{t+1}>=Confidence_t regardless of evidence as unacceptable, requiring instead Confidence_{t+1}=Update(Confidence_t,E_{t+1}) with decreases allowed and expected when evidence warrants. Separately warns of epistemic hysteresis: a system at Confidence=0.99 that moves only to 0.98 upon contradictory evidence may be statistically unjustified -- the update mechanism must have explicit responsiveness." (anchor: "No irreversible confidence inflation; epistemic hysteresis warning")
- `[S0942]` types=[FORMALIZATION, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "For theta_{t+1}=theta_t+alpha_t*Delta_t, too-large alpha_t creates oscillation and too-small alpha_t creates sluggish adaptation. Every learned update should record LearningMethod so K_{t+1} can answer how the change was produced, represented as K_t --Evidence,Method,Policy--> K_{t+1}, making the update operation itself auditable." (anchor: "Learning rate tradeoff; heterogeneous (non-gradient-descent) learning operators; mandatory learning provenance")
